title: DP I: Linear / 1D (LIS, Coin Change, House-Robber, 1D Knapsack)
relevance: High (the single most reused OA/interview DP family — fib stairs, rob houses, coin change, subset-sum knapsack, LIS)
company_notes: Stairs/tickets/days (min cost with 1/7/30-day passes) → Frog / Climbing Stairs (Amazon, Uber). Loot / delete-and-earn (taking x deletes x±1) → House Robber on a frequency axis (FAANG screens). Fewest coins or number of combinations → unbounded knapsack (nearly every OA bank). Equal skill-sum split or max value under budget W → 0/1 knapsack / Partition Equal Subset Sum (Google, Microsoft, product companies).

phases.goal: Confirm the candidate maps signal wording to 1D index DP rather than grid/interval/bitmask families.

must_hit.point: State lives on a 1D index (position, sum, value, or length) with local transitions: take/skip, extend a prior sum by a coin/item, or append to a better prior subsequence.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says dp is indexed by i/sum/value/length and transitions only use nearby prior states.

must_hit.point: Signal words include number of ways / min coins to make a sum, max points if adjacent choices conflict, subset with sum = half / capacity W, or longest increasing subsequence.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names at least two of those phrases as the cue for this family.

must_hit.point: If dp[i] only needs dp[i-1], dp[i-2], or a loop over coins/items into a sum array, the problem belongs in linear/1D DP.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the i-1/i-2 window or coin-into-sum-array shape as the membership test.

must_hit.point: Delete-and-earn / Boredom-style "taking x deletes neighbors" is House Robber after mapping values to points on a frequency axis.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps value-axis loot wording to freq then rob.

probes: What wording or recurrence shape makes you pick linear/1D DP over grid or interval DP?
How do stairs, adjacent-conflict loot, coin change, equal partition, and LIS each signal this family?

hints.1: Look at whether the state is a single index and transitions are local.
hints.2: Match signal phrases: ways/min coins, adjacent conflict, half-sum/capacity W, LIS; or dp needing only i-1/i-2 or a coin loop.
hints.3: Say: 1D index DP; take/skip or coin-into-sum or LIS append; if only i-1/i-2 or coins into a sum array, it is this family; delete-and-earn is freq-axis House Robber.

phases.goal: Get the candidate to name the right 1D template before coding: take/skip, unbounded vs 0/1 knapsack, or LIS.

must_hit.point: Adjacent conflict / House Robber / Boredom uses take/skip: dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], dp[i-2] + a[i]).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Writes or states that exact take/skip recurrence.

must_hit.point: Unbounded coin change uses dp[x] = min(dp[x-c]) + 1 (or ways analog); loop order decides permutations vs combinations.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States min-coins recurrence and that outer-sum/inner-coins vs outer-coins/inner-sum flips permutation vs combination counting.

must_hit.point: 0/1 knapsack / Partition Equal Subset Sum is boolean or count DP to a target (often sum/2), each item used at most once.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names subset-sum/partition to sum/2 or capacity W with 0/1 use.

must_hit.point: LIS is either ending-at-i DP or patience-sorting tails with lower_bound; House Robber II reduces a circle to two linear House Robber runs.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions O(n^2) ending-at-i and/or tails+lower_bound, and circle→two linears.

probes: Before coding, which template is this: take/skip, unbounded coins, 0/1 subset-sum, or LIS?
For coins, how do you choose loop order? For a circular robber, how do you reduce it?

hints.1: Classify adjacent conflict vs coins vs partition vs LIS.
hints.2: Take/skip uses i-1 vs i-2+a[i]; coins need the min/ways recurrence and loop-order meaning; partition targets sum/2; circle→two linear robs.
hints.3: Say: max(dp[i-1], dp[i-2]+a[i]); dp[x]=min(dp[x-c])+1 with outer-sum→permutations vs outer-coin→combinations; 0/1 to sum/2; LIS ending-at-i or tails+lower_bound; HR II = two linear runs.

phases.goal: Verify the candidate can write the standard 1D templates, rolling arrays, and reconstruction pointers.

must_hit.point: Implement House Robber / Boredom take/skip and Climbing Stairs fib ways dp[i]=dp[i-1]+dp[i-2].
In a 1D 0/1 knapsack array, iterate capacity downward so each item is used at most once; Book Shop–style rolling array is fine.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States downward capacity loop for 0/1 correctness.

must_hit.point: Coin Combinations: outer sum, inner coins → permutations; outer coins, inner sum → combinations (order fixed).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States both nestings and which counting they produce.

must_hit.point: For path/subsequence reconstruction store prev[i] (or parent pointers) beside dp[i]; space-optimize fib/rob/frog to O(1) or O(K) when only a window is needed.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions prev pointers and window-only space.

probes: Write the take/skip and min-coins skeletons, and the 0/1 downward capacity loop.
How do you nest coin loops for combinations vs permutations, and how do you reconstruct a path?

hints.1: Start from rob/stairs and the coin min update.
hints.2: Add downward capacity for 0/1; separate the two coin nestings; keep prev for reconstruction.
hints.3: Say: max(skip, take prior); dp[i]=dp[i-1]+dp[i-2]; downward 1D 0/1; outer-sum=perms, outer-coin=combs; prev[i] for indices; keep O(1)/O(K) window if possible.

phases.goal: State the LIS costs and when to flip knapsack dimensions or shrink space to a window.

must_hit.point: LIS has both O(n^2) ending-at-i DP and O(n log n) tails + lower_bound (patience sorting).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Quotes both O(n^2) and O(n log n) LIS approaches.

must_hit.point: When only a window of prior states is needed, space-optimize fib / rob / frog to O(1) or O(K).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says drop the full array to constant or K previous states.

must_hit.point: If weight capacity is 10^9 but values are small, flip to DP on value and store min weight (Knapsack 2 style).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names flipping the dimension when W is 10^9 and sum of values is small.

probes: What complexities do you quote for the two LIS templates?
When do you shrink to O(1)/O(K) space, and when do you flip knapsack off of weight?

hints.1: Separate LIS asymptotic options from space tricks.
hints.2: O(n^2) vs O(n log n) LIS; window→O(1)/O(K); huge W→DP on value.
hints.3: Say: LIS O(n^2) ending-at-i and O(n log n) tails+lower_bound; fib/rob/frog → O(1) or O(K); if W is 10^9 and values small, DP value → min weight.

phases.goal: Catch wrong coin nesting, upward 0/1 updates, odd-sum partitions, and missing reconstruction/circle handling.

must_hit.point: Mixing coin loop order: outer sum/inner coins counts permutations; outer coins/inner sum counts combinations—swapping them silently wrong-counts ways.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explains the permutation vs combination nesting trap.

must_hit.point: Iterating capacity upward in a 1D 0/1 knapsack reuses the same item; must go downward.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names upward iteration as the classic double-use bug.

must_hit.point: Equal partition is impossible when sum is odd; otherwise target sum/2 with boolean/count DP.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Checks odd sum first, then knapsack to sum/2.

must_hit.point: Forgetting prev[i] when asked to reconstruct indices, or treating circular House Robber as one linear pass instead of two.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions parent pointers and the two-run circular reduction.

probes: What breaks if your coin loops or 1D 0/1 direction are wrong?
When is equal partition immediately impossible, and what do circular robber / reconstruction need?

hints.1: Check loop nesting, capacity direction, and parity of sum.
hints.2: Outer-sum vs outer-coin; downward 0/1; odd sum→impossible; circle needs two runs; keep prev.
hints.3: List: wrong nesting → perms/combs swapped; upward 1D 0/1 reuses items; odd sum blocks equal partition; HR II = two linear runs; store prev[i] to rebuild.

tradeoffs.topic: Coin Combinations I vs II (outer sum/inner coins vs outer coins/inner sum)
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Outer sum then inner coins counts permutations of coins; outer coins then inner sum counts combinations with order fixed—same unbounded knapsack family, different nesting for the ask.

tradeoffs.topic: LIS O(n^2) ending-at-i DP vs O(n log n) tails + lower_bound
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Ending-at-i DP is the clear interview explanation; patience-sorting tails with lower_bound is the O(n log n) template CSES forces when n is larger.
Classic DP indexes by weight/capacity; when W is 10^9 but values are small, flip state to value and store min weight.

tradeoffs.topic: Full dp array vs O(1)/O(K) window
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Keep the full array when you need all states or reconstruction aids; if only dp[i-1]/dp[i-2] or a jump window of K is used, shrink to O(1) or O(K) previous states.

gotchas.trap: Using the wrong coin-loop nesting and reporting the wrong 'number of ways'.
gotchas.correction: Outer sum, inner coins → permutations; outer coins, inner sum → combinations.

gotchas.trap: 1D 0/1 knapsack iterating capacity upward so an item is reused.
gotchas.correction: Iterate capacity downward so each item is used at most once.

gotchas.trap: Attempting equal partition without checking parity.
gotchas.correction: If sum is odd, answer is impossible; otherwise run subset-sum to sum/2.

gotchas.trap: Solving circular House Robber with a single linear pass.
gotchas.correction: Reduce the circle to two linear House Robber runs.

gotchas.trap: Computing only lengths/values when the ask needs the actual subsequence or path.
gotchas.correction: Store prev[i] or parent pointers alongside dp[i] and walk them back.
